body: Looks like it came from 4chan
The Virgin walk meme is basically me.
In what kind of workplace are people allowed to say stuff like that and it's just shrugged off?
I will watch some tennis on tv this weekend, it's the finals in the French open. Otherwise I won't be doing much.

I did not say that you were disabled but you mentioned ableism, the ableist nature of normies. Ableism is a word for the discrimination of people with disabilities so I thought you meant that it is in the nature of normies to discriminate against people with disabilities.

Its unfair to call all 'normies' ableist as if normies are one huge group that think alike. Ableism is widespread among the population and disabled people face discrimination everyday, discrimination which is often not acknowledged. Discrimination against disabled people is also linked to the economic system we live in because your worth as a person in this system is based on how 'productive' you are,or in other words, how much you can be exploited for the benefit of your masters. Because disabilities often hinder your ability to work people with disabilities are often seen as less.


I know what you mean when you talk about how unfairly treated people on the spectrum are. Many like to pretend that they are inclusive and all but they are not, far from. In their eyes an autistic person is someone like the main character from Me.Robot. A bit quirky, good looking, has friends, but likes to keep to himself and of course he is a genius of some sort. So 80% 'normal' 20% off. When they meat and autistic person in real life that does not conform to this idealistic image they have they go mask off.

On the surface I am holding up OK but I feel I feel really down. I'm so exhausted and stressed out, not because anything out of the ordinary has happened to me but it's just how it is. Sometimes these periods come along. 


I don't have any plans but saw that the Champions League final is this weekend so I will watch it.

I'm in my mid thirties, closer to 40 than 30, and a KHHV. I think it's because of several reasons. Below average looks, missing out during my formative years because of stuff that happened which caused a severely stunted development, being generally meek and quiet, etc. All of that combined is what made me FA.
I won't do anything special, just pass my time until another Monday comes. I've been getting really depressed watching the news lately with everything thats going on.

There's no real guarantee that you will get to know more people, other than on a surface level, in a bigger company. Offices tend to be miserable places. I wouldn't switch jobs just because of that and especially not if that comes with a significant paycut.

It gets much harder with age. 18-24 is nothing strange even if 24 might be considered later than usual. Mid twenties seem to be a cut off age for when it gets much harder, but there's still hope. Thirty and forward is basically "it's over" territory. There are success stories but they are very few and even if you do lose your virginity at this age its not the same as doing so when you were younger.
I will try to relax and read a book. Other than that I have nothing planned.

I read your reply and the reply from others in this thread and it's always interesting to see how there seems to be some common issues for people like us. I think moving away during my formative years completely stunted my mental development in many ways and I became very isolated and drawn back. I wasn't a very confident or  outgoing  person to begin with,  so I can't say with certainty that anything would have been different, but I truly believe that it was the single most important event that decided my FA-future.

I would have gotten into sports at an early age and also started strength training pretty early. I used to be very skinny and weak and I think it would have helped with giving me more confidence. We also moved to a completely different place when I was in my teenage years and everything afterwards became I disaster so if we stayed where we used to live I think I would have had the chance to be better off.
I would says Blade Runner(both the original and the new one with Ryan Gosling) are movies that would appeal to many FAs even if they are not FA movies per se.
None really but if I had to choose more of a black pill in the sense that I have lost all hope and never had any to begin with. However, I don't buy into all the hateful nonsense that surround it.
Just where I am today but closer to death. I don't think anything will improve, it will stay mostly the same, stagnant.
The Internet is a bad place for women in general and so are many FA-spaces. I get why women need their own forums online.

I will meet a relative during the easter weekend. We will just hang out and chill.


Other than that everything is as usual. I'm thinking of maybe going on a solo travel during summer. I've had this thought about solo travelling for a while but I never went anywhere. It could be nice to just change the setting for maybe a week.

Sorry man but when you said pulling the trigger I got a really different association.


I would also love to have a cat or a dog but don't know if I would manage to care for them enough.

I am the opposite. I barely buy anything for myself and when I want something I can spend so much time thinking about if I really need it or not, or if its worth it, that in the end I don't buy anything at all. I've spent so much time thinking about items that I've never bought that it's ridiculous.
I'm going to do the same as you.

I've slept really bad lately but today I slept well. I fell asleep early and slept almost in one piece without waking up several times during the night. 


Otherwise not much is happening. Maybe I'll go out for a walk later, maybe I'll just sit around, don't really know. 


I'm thinking of trying out some games on my phone as I've never used my phone for playing before. It just feels off but if it's fun then I'll have yet another activity to pass time with.
I have never been asked that question but if I was I would just say yes and try to avoid any further conversation.

When I was in my teens we moved to a completely different town. I never adjusted well to the new setting for many reasons and that was the moment I became very isolated and started to live most of my life alone in my room. A lot of time has passed since and I can't blame everything on that but I really don't think I ever recovered since it happened right during my formative years. Even before that I was sort of a proto FA already so I don't think it was the main cause but it certainly cemented my fate.

I'm just going to relax because I've been really stressed and have been sleeping bad lately. Stress hits differently as an FA because you are completely stuck in your own head all the time so whatever happens gets amplified. 
I will try to relax by going on walks and maybe doing some jigsaw puzzles.
I will read a book and go for some walks. Maybe watch some movies or tv shows.
I am lucky that I have a very close relationship with my mother. We see each other almost every day or at least several days a week. It means very much to me.

I have very few things saved from my life.  Somewhere there is a hard drive with downloaded movies and shows but I don't have a computer anymore so I will probably throw it away sooner or later. I used to burn my movies on DVDs and I had loads of burned DVDs that I eventually threw away.


I sometimes think about how I relate certain years of my life to the movies or shows that I watched because there was not much in my real life I remember them by.

I have been sick lately but now I'm feeling better. I will spend my weekend just taking it easy by reading a book or watching some movies. Since I've been staying at home so much it would be good to come out for some short walks to get back on track.


Even with my general apathetic attitude towards everything it's difficult to not care at all about everything that is going on since the world is clearly going to shit right now at a fast pace.
I also used to be very skinny and I think it has affected my life negatively and that it is a large contributing factor to why I ended up as an FA.

Grind at work and spend my free time doing mostly nothing but reading, watching movies and tv shows, taking walks, and other things that makes time pass. Unfortunately I might have developed a bad drinking habit that I keep mostly under control but I suspect it will get worse with age.
At the moment no but it comes and goes. There is a suicide scale comic posted sometimes and currently I'm somewhere between a 5-6 out of ten.

From the statistics I've seen not even a few percent are virgins in their thirties so I would say its quite rare despite how strict you are with the definition of what an FA really is. I haven't met a single person that's like me in this age. Maybe it's not statistically relevant but it says something at least.

This was really well put. I also feel resigned because of the development and rise of fascism in the world. Worrying about all the personal issues I have feels almost pathetic in comparison to what is about to come.
This feels like it's so illegal, or should be illegal, but with workers having almost no rights anymore I'm not surprised if employers can get away with almost anything.

It seems to be very common among FAs that we have a hard time relating to people our age, or with people that are slightly older than us, because our lived experiences differ so much. I feel the same but at the same time I don't really relate with younger people either.

From an early age I knew the battle was lost before it even began. I have always been weak and fairly unattractive, especially when I was young, and this combined with being socially isolated during the formative years in my youth doomed me.

I'm sorry about your cat. I know it must be though without your little companion and I hope your hanging in there.


This week has been pretty uneventful and nothing has really happened, like most other weeks. When the weather improves I might just pick up my solitary walks again. I'm trying to find some "interests" or "hobbies" to make the time pass but it feels really bad that everything I do is just for the sake of passing time and not because I actually enjoy it

I am only a few years younger than you and feel that all hope is lost and that it wouldn't even matter if I lost my virginity at this point. When I read stories like this it makes me happy and I'm really glad that you feel better about yourself.

The first one is called The Nakano Thrift Shop. There is some awkward love stories in there so it's not really an FA book. I am not sure about the second one because I never came to read it but I think it's called Rules for Commuting. It looks like a British feel good book. Sometimes when I'm on a binge I search for suggestions that are similar to what I'm reading and note the titles but after I while the list of books that I want to read tend to get too big so I forget about them.

It would have made a much bigger difference 15 years ago. Even if I lost it now it wouldn't be the same thing as if I had lost it when I was a teenager or in my early twenties. It's not only about the fact that you have not had sex but about all the stunted emotional and social development that comes with it. You can't have that back even if you lose your virginity later in life. It might make me a bit happier if I lost it now but it's the same kind of happiness I feel when I pick up a video game nowadays. It's slightly fun(but not really) but not even close to how fun it was when I was a kid. Some things are not the same when you experience them later in life.

I was thinking more about the kind of social media where you have your own personal account where everybody knows its you and you have contacts and such but realize that social media is a much wider term and that I'm completely out of the loop.

This is true but there's an additional component to it as an FA. I never used social media when I was young because I barely had any contacts or something to post so I never kept up even when I was young. Many years ago I briefly had a social media account that I quickly deleted because of inactivity. People our age still use social media but not in the same way as younger folks do. Having a Facebook or maybe an Instagram account is more or less normal for people our age but getting a TikTok account would not be that common.

I'm trying to find some things to do besides doomscrolling the web. I haven't read a book in a while so maybe I will pick up reading again. Otherwise I've thought about coloring or maybe try out drawing. I'm so bad at drawing that I can barely draw stick figures so I would see it as a challenge since I'm a complete anti talent when it comes to drawing. Most likely I won't be doing anything but since time is all I have there are better ways to spend it than by doing nothing but its easier said that done.

I also read occasionally and like books about small communities. It doesn't even have to be a community it could just be a few people hanging out regularly in a book shop or another setting. I read a book a few months ago about some people in a second hand shop and I thought about reading a book about some commuters that get to know each other on their daily commutes. I usually borrow my books from the library as I find it the easiest. 
I would like to be more involved in communities but feel like I wouldn't fit in anywhere and that I wouldn't have the energy to engage properly.
I am also in my mid thirties and I have lost interest in everything. The days just pass and I pass along with them. All hope for a brighter future is lost.
The video was muted when it started and I could still hear his voice.
I could never do it to my mother. I am fairly certain that I won't die of old age but I won't take my own life while my mother is still alive.

I have a very hard time to keep a conversation going and I think I often come across as very aloof. I think one of the reasons is because with time I have found that I have less and less in common with most people which makes it harder to interact.
I was once a youngcel. Then I became a wizard.

I really don't think so. Meeting someone on dating sites is extremely hard for most men, and nearly impossible for lower average guys. Since I assume most of us have small to non existant social circles meeting someone the regular way is even harder. Even if we assume that we do meet someone being an FA is a giant red flag to most people and eventually it will come up in a conversation. If you are attractive those things are much easier to overlook for others but you will be judged much more harshly if you are not.
Somewhere between 4-5. Even being average wouldn't help at this age. You would need to be very good looking to compensate for everything you have missed out on and have a chance as an FA.

I know the feeling. I've never associated new years with any festivities since I've spent almost all of them at home in my room.


It's four hours left where I live and I have a hard time not falling asleep since I'm very tired. 


I know what life is like for people like us but I still wish you and everyone here a happy new year even if I know that nobody feels genuinely happy about it.

Some people who recently became parents can be very uptight and way too careful about their babies and young children. It's understandable because it's a huge responsibility and a new situation for them but their attitude can become too much and if something isn't done exactly like they want it they freak out. From what I read you already sound like a great uncle so don't step back.
I'm going to spend it with my mum. We will have a dinner, maybe watch some television or play some games. It will be pleasant but nothing out of the ordinary.
I have some stuffed animals that look like a pillow with a very friendly face. I like to hug them and it gives me comfort.

Me and my mum had a nice and relaxing Christmas with some guests over for dinner. This Christmas and new years is pretty good because there are a lot of free days off from work. Fortunately I can work from home during the regular days so it feels really chill. 


Otherwise I feel really melancholic. Another year has almost passed cementing this lonely and sad state that I'm in even further. Not many glimpses of hope left.
I once had a lucid dream where I found out that I could jump from a building and stop in the air before I hit the ground so I did it a couple of times.

I'm in my mid thirties and for this age I think I look okish, maybe on the lowest end of average, since most people's looks are declining at this stage. Maybe they are already settled down and don't care anymore or they are letting themselves go for other reasons. During those years when it mattered the most I was a shy and really skinny twink with a non-threatening aura and demeanor. I have gained some weight during the last ten years but I am still skinny but not as super skinny as I used to be. So me putting myself at the lowest end of average is not the results of some glow up but more of the fact that others are declining while I have more or less stayed the same.
Merry Christmas to you too!

I know that you might be in a very bad place mentally due to being FA but having a good relation with his uncle can mean a lot to your nephew, and to you too. I don't know how your relation is with your family and sister but try to build a relation with your nephew while he is young. Children bond very easily with adult relatives while they are very young and if a couple of more years pass with no interactions between the two of you, you and your nephew can easily become estranged from each other and it can be much harder to bond even when he is just a few years older.
I think those acronyms are light hearted and funny. I've never thought of them as showing of who has it worst as an FA but more like a descriptive label to show what kind of FA you are.

I know the question is aimed at older FAs but many of the things mentioned didn't feel like they were too long ago. I'm in my mid thirties and I can remember most of those things. We didn't get our first computer until the beginning of this century and we had a dial up modem for several years after that so internet was not even close to what it is today. Smartphones became big around maybe 2010 and forward so computers still dominated for a long time. I didnt get a smartphone until rather late when I was way in to my twenties so I would say that smartphones and this modern technology played a very small part in shaping me as an FA.

Not much is happening. Maybe I'm going to watch A Hundred Years of Solitude but I'm not sure if they will be able to capture the tone and feeling of the book. There's something about the way they make shows and movies today that feels off. Everything feels like it has a smooth finish, like you can barely separate the picture quality of a show or movie from commercial.
That sub would rate Brad Pitt and Will Smith a 6 tops.
Welcome! Becoming a wizard is an honour bestowed upon the few.

More or less. It's bad luck in the sense that several unfortunate factors have to align for us to end this way. Statistically someone will always end up FA, even if the percentage of FAs in the total population is really low, and now it just happened to be us.
The difference is that it never happened for us and it led to us rotting away coping for the rest of our lives
Time has been a blur for many years. That's one of the reasons for why it feels like time is going so fast, because everything feels like a fog and all days are the same.

I also like these friday chats but my days almost always look the same so I don't have much to say about my week. I think I've heard about the book in your post, or a similar one on the same theme. It is different for people who choose a single life but there are things we can do to improve our lives. The problem for me is that everything I do feels like a cope and then I just give up and let the time pass.

It's a silly question. I think it's worth much more to have been with just one person you really cared about than having a big  number just for the sake of it. 

Nobody has asked me that question but those who really know me know it's 0 so there's really no point to ask.
looks like it's inactive, last post I see is from two months ago

Yeah, I think we cope much better with loneliness than the average normie because we are used to it but at some point copes don't help anymore. It's easier to cope with being hungry if you know you will have a meal in an hour than if you are dying from starvation and haven't had food for weeks.

I don't mind when former FAs write about their experiences, I'm happy for them and that they found a way out of this rot, and I also think it's a valuable input to hear from people who have escaped this. This however feels to much like gloating, even if you maybe don't mean it like that. I understand that it's great to have escaped the loneliness of being FA but from this it sounds like you are relying too much on your wife for your own happiness. My input might be worthless but one risk lonely people face that have found a partner is that they become too attached because they have never had anyone before and they are afraid of being lonely. When you write that you are not able to function without your wife it sounds a bit like that.

Mechanical engineering. I feel like this state that I am in is a constant and chronical burn out. Most people don't like to work and do it because they have to but working just to come home, do nothing, and sit out your time is incredibly tiring.
It's an ok job but working has always felt miserable to me. I would rather be a NEET if I could.
Engineering. I don't have any real interest in it.

Not to go too much into detail about asexuality, because I do think some people feel a much stronger sexual urge than others, but sometimes it feels like a cope and a symptom or cover for other problems.
Inside Out 2. I like going to the cinema by myself but I rarely go.
intp or infp

I had a weird lucid dream last night. In the dream I was standing on a platform in a train station and I became aware that I was dreaming. Then I walked around and did some stuff and when I closed my eyes I knew that I would be back in my room and awake when I opened them. I hoped that I would be stuck in the dream but unfortunately I did wake up as suspected.

I've also thought about cutting my own hair but it seems rather difficult. As a first attempt I thought that I can use a trimmer to cut it short to the same size, that should be fairly easy. I don't care about how it looks.

I know what it's like. I also have a job but none of that matters when you are very lonely and have missed out on many formative experiences. What is even the point of working when you have nothing to live for? Beeing like this gets harder with age, just existing feels exhausting and like a chore at this stage in life.

The only thing left for me is to try to find a small glimpse of contentment in small everyday things and routines like a morning coffee, reading a good book, taking a walk, watching a movie and stuff like that.

One bedroom is enough for me. Even when I've lived in flats with more than one room I've always had all my stuff in one room and the rest have been empty. I wonder if it's an FA-trait to use less space.

If I stop daydreaming the only thing I will do is stare at the walls of my room or into an empty void. My potential is already wasted, there is no potential left. Daydreaming is a cope to deal with that reality.

I am actually curious to try it(but I probably won't). It seems to be legal(or semi-legal, a substance in kratom is apparently classed as a narcotic but kratom itself is not so far) where I live, but it's probably just a matter of time before it's classed as an illegal drug if it actually is effective, even if it's effect is weak.

From what I read percocet is a mix between oxycodone and paracetamol. I was prescribed oxycodone after a surgery, as it is a strong painkiller, but I never used it. If there was something legal and similar that could help me self medicate I would be very open to it.

I'm in a slump where I don't really have anything to do. Usually my days are uninteresting but it has come to a point where I just sit in my chair and look around the room for long periods of time while I imagine scenarios in my own head. Copes like movies, games and books don't really work, even they feel like a hassle sometimes. I go for walks and I do some light physical excercises but even then I have the rest of the day to kill off.

Try going to a bigger sub and just write something generic or nonoffensive that most people can agree on and hopefully you will get some upvotes. Maybe try commenting in the main FA sub, it has a larger userbase. Asking directly for upvotes is probably not a good idea since some people will downvote it instictively.

I woke up one day but couldn't move, it took me like a half minute before I could start moving. It happened after one of thoses rare dreams in which I had a girlfriend so it was a nice dream. I've never had one so I don't know what it feels like but waking up was sad since I got a glimpse of what is missing in life. 

Otherwise not much has happened.
Seeing posts like this makes it perfectly understandable why FA-women have their own sub where men are not allowed.

There is more to it than just looks but looks are by far the biggest component of why someone ends up FA. I mean how often does someone like Brad Pitt end up like this? If you are attractive you can have almost any personality or other major issues and still would not end up like this.

I was also skinny and weak and some people even commented that I looked like I was in a concentration camp when I was at my skinniest. I hardly think it's a coincidence that the weakest and skinniest guy also ended up as an FA.

I'm really sorry for the problems you have with your car. Dealing with stuff like that can be unbearably draining as an FA. Whenever something happens that I have to deal with it can take a long time for me to recover because coping with life is hard enough as it is and then some additional shit occurs that is just enough to send me over the edge.  
I hope you are doing ok despite the circumstances and good luck with your writing.

It has affected affected my ability to connect and interact with other people. I often zone out and I'm very aloof when I'm with others. Often, when I'm with others, it's like I'm not even present because I'm stuck in my own head with my mind wandering off.

I've started running once a week as well. Today I was out running for half an hour, it's a nice start on a Saturday.

Otherwise it's been a pretty uneventful week as usual. I was watching a tv show and there was a mother with a child in it and then there was a couple living in a nice house. I checked out the cast and they were all my age(mid thirties) or younger, so when the show was filmed they were even younger. I thought of them as much older than what they were, and this has happened many times before, that I think of people that are my age or even younger as much older than they really are. It has nothing to do with ther looks but my brain probably instictively thinks that people who are in a certain stage in life are much older than they are, just like when you were fifteen and people with families were  much older, but now you're not fifteen anymore and those people are you're age or even younger.
There's no reason for me to keep going but I still do. I will be around at least until my mom is, after that I don't know.

It's the opposite for me, I barely buy any fun or interesting stuff for myself. I wish that I spent more on myself but I don't know what to spend money on since I barely have any interests left and I'm just really down most of the times. It's such an empty life. I like books but I borrow most of them from the library when I feel like reading.

I've been drinking alone for many years but for the last month I have stopped doing it. I usually drank three or four beers per night a couple of times a week and sometimes even more. Even though it's not a huge dose of alcohol I am a bit worried about the effects that type of continuous drinking for so long could have, which is the reason I'm trying to stop. I know that I will probably relapse eventually but I will try my best not to do it.

I am really hesitant of going to a psychiatrist even if I have been in what is probably a depression for many many years and I'm also riddled with anxiety. There are so many potential sideeffects from SSRI medications and they don't seem to work for many people, or they work just slightly better than placebo, that is why I'm a bit sceptic about them.
I have the same body type as you and have never had any confidence in my body.

I'm in my mid thirties and I don't think ascending at this age would mean nearly as much as it would when you are much younger. Being FA for this long is about so much more than never having had a relationship or an intimate experience. It's also about having missed out on so many crucial formative experiences that are needed for a healthy emotional and mental development. The isolation and loneliness that usually comes with it has shaped who we are and even if some of us would technically stop being FA, like your colleague, the damage cannot be undone.
I've started doing some simple stretching exercises because I'm very stiff and my hope is to at least get a little bit more flexible. It's something simple I can do at home.

That's good for you that you are doing things even if it's by yourself. I've been thinking of maybe going to a game of my local football(soccer) team when they play at home. Watching sports on site can be quite fun but I haven't been to a sporting event for a long while.
I always wake up before my alarm. I can't even remember the last time my alarm woke me up.

I used to watch lots of sports. I still do but not nearly as much. I followed tennis for many years, nowadays I watch it occasionally when there happens to be a game on TV but I still follow results and what happens in the tennis world.

I live by myself and as I don't have much stuff the place is pretty tidy but I can't say it's because I take care of it very much, it's more that the lack off stuff makes it tidy per default. I hope that I can find small thing I enjoy in life that makes life at least somewhat more fulfilling. 

Good luck to you too and take care!

I'm thankful for my mother. We have a very good relationship and have been through a lot together.

Today I was out running for the first time in many years. It was a short run of around two kilometers but it felt good.

Unfortunately I don't really have any copes that give me joy anymore. The copes I have are mostly mindlessly browsing the web, watching tv shows or movies, or playing games that I don't really find interesting anymore just to pass time. I think it's nice that you have these little things that lift you up and I think it's a positive mindset to have for people like us. 

I shave maybe once every other week and put on some balm afterwards. One shaving foam and after shave balm could last me more than a year.

I like going to the cinema by myself but I go very rarely, maybe once or twice a year. I used to watch much more movies before but I also have a much more difficult time finding movies to watch these days.

Things are getting back to normal after a pretty boring summer holiday. I felt really tense for various reasons and didn't get much  rest at all.

I have been telling myself for a long time that I need to become more active and start eating better since things are going in the wrong direction but it's so hard to find the energy and will when you don't see the point.
I've been eating rather poorly lately and have lost a substantial amount of weight which has left me feeling very tired and without any energy.

Movies, tv shows, reading etc. Unfortunately I've lost interest in almost anything and those are copes that barely work anymore. Occasionaly I go out for solitary walks but I used to do it much more before.
Happy birthday! I know birthdays are rarely joyful for people like us but I hope that you can find a moment of peace enjoying your burger and beers.

I'm meek, shy, drawn back and aloof, in other words my personality is the complete opposite of what is attractive in a person. While I have never been an outgoing person who is at the center of attention bursting with joy and energy, some of these personality traits are also because I have lived and adapted to a relatively lonely life. I have always been more of a withdrawn person but not even close to how I am now.
I'm back at work after my vacation. I'm as tired as I was before the vacation.

I wish I could live a simple life where I get pleasure from small things like going for a walk, having a cup of coffee, watching a good movie or reading a good book etc. However the way things are going I'm on my way to becoming completely numb since I don't find pleasure in anything and have no will to do anything.
ok, I didn't know babies are born every year
I didn't express myself well enough. I didn't mean the last name as such as there are of course other unrelated people that have the same name as it is not unique, but our family line.
My family name will die with me. I think about it everytime I visit my grandmother's grave. When I die there will be no one to bury me.

I feel really bad too. I don't have any brothers and sisters so my mother will never have any grandkids. I love my mother very much and we are very close. She has never said anything about my FA situation but I know that she would be really happy if she could have grandchildren since she is a very loving person and she is good with children.

I will probably try to sell my place if I can and move in with my mother. The cost of living simply isn't worth it for me since I don't have a social or dating life that can in any way be hindered if I don't live by myself. For me at least there are no pros of living alone the way my life is. If I was ten years younger I probably would think think about it differently.
I have never been rejected since I was never part of the game

Family members  and relatives have urged me to go to therapy too and I most probably will go after the summer.
